title: VIAM Machine Configuration
subtitle: Unlocking data & AI in the physical world

overview: Viam has been working since 2019 to create a new standard for hobbyist developers to Fortune 500 businesses to configure, launch, control, and monitor their fleets of IoT and robotic devices.

To leverage the full power of Viam's ecosystem of products, from data aggregation to machine learning models to a registry of compliant components, users need a way to efficiently configure and test their new smart machines.
Machine configuration acts as the core of the VIAM platform, and other product services such as Fleet Management, Data, Machine Learning, & Registry derive their ecosystem-level value from it.

sections.label: The Challenge
sections.headline: Years of rapid growth left the platform fragmented.

cards.text: Design and technical debt accumulated from years of feature additions without consolidation.
Developer tooling lacked familiar UI patterns, making adoption slow for enterprise teams.
Creation and configuration flows were disjointed, forcing users through confusing multi-step processes.

cards.title: Increased enterprise adoption
cards.description: Make the platform feel mature and trustworthy for Fortune 500 teams.

cards.title: Reduced configuration time
cards.description: Cut setup friction for solutions engineers onboarding new customers.

cards.title: Familiar developer patterns
cards.description: Mirror conventions from VS Code and modern dev tools to flatten the learning curve.

features.name: Tree Navigation
features.headline: Your machine, mapped out.
features.description: Manage machines and sub-parts with an intuitive hierarchical structure. Navigate complex configurations with ease and understand relationships between components at a glance.

features.name: JSON Editing
features.headline: Code when you need it.
features.description: Power users get granular configuration through direct code access. Switch seamlessly between visual and code editing for maximum flexibility and control.

features.name: Null States
features.headline: Never start from zero.
features.description: New users receive friendly guidance and contextual help at every step. Empty states become opportunities for learning, not barriers to progress.

features.name: Logs
features.headline: See what's happening, live.
features.description: Access real-time diagnostics and feedback directly in the interface. Identify issues instantly and understand exactly what your machine is doing.

features.name: Connect Tab
features.headline: From config to code in seconds.
features.description: Get auto-generated boilerplate code for quick integration. Copy, paste, and start building. No more hunting through documentation.

sections.title: Trade-offs
sections.label: Trade-offs
sections.headline: What we cut, and why it mattered.

items.title: Dual-mode over wizard
items.description: Chose visual + JSON editing instead of a step-by-step wizard. Protected power users who needed granular control while still offering a visual interface for beginners. Trade-off: slightly steeper initial learning curve for new users, but avoided the 'wizard trap' where advanced users hit a ceiling.

items.title: Phased launch deprioritized
items.description: Shipped all features together in 4 months instead of breaking into phases. Prioritized delivering a cohesive experience over faster initial delivery. Trade-off: Later launch date, but avoided fragmented user experience and rework costs.

items.title: Template library postponed
items.description: Cut pre-built configuration templates from v1 to ship on schedule. Focused on making the core configuration workflow 65% faster instead. Relied on null states + contextual help rather than template library. Trade-off: users start from scratch, but the core flow is so fast it's still net-positive.

items.title: Advanced filtering deferred
items.description: Deprioritized complex filtering in tree navigation to focus on hierarchical clarity. Bet that clear structure would reduce the need for search/filter. Trade-off: users with 50+ components may need to scroll more, but 90% of users have simpler setups where hierarchy is sufficient.

sections.title: Systems Thinking
sections.label: Ecosystem Impact
sections.headline: How configuration changes ripple through the platform.

items.title: Fleet Management coordination
items.description: Machine configuration feeds fleet-level data. Improved tree navigation meant fleet managers could now understand machine hierarchies without switching contexts. Coordinated with Fleet team to ensure config changes didn't break their dashboards. Reduced cross-team support tickets by enabling self-service troubleshooting.

items.title: Data pipeline quality
items.description: Better configuration UX led to more accurate component setup, which meant cleaner data flowing to ML models. Logs feature caught misconfigurations before they corrupted datasets. Data team reported fewer 'garbage in, garbage out' edge cases after launch.

items.title: Registry ecosystem trust
items.description: Enterprise customers evaluate the platform by configuration experience first. VS Code-style patterns increased enterprise confidence in the entire registry ecosystem. Helped close deals with Tennibot and Billion Oyster Project by demonstrating production readiness.

items.title: Engineering support efficiency
items.description: 65% faster configuration meant solutions engineers onboarded new customers faster. Connect tab (auto-generated code) removed documentation bottleneck. Engineering team shifted from reactive support to proactive feature development.
